boundaryJustification.startWhy: Event 1191 begins the comparison that connects biological design to theism and leads directly into the architect-only limitation at events 1200–1203.

boundaryJustification.removedPrefix: Events 1180–1190 were removed because they recount prior work, assert Darwinism came up short, and promote books rather than establish this burden-limiting concession.

boundaryJustification.startWhy: Event 1386 begins the substantive support for evolved visual structures by introducing published accounts of the eye's different evolutionary pathways.

boundaryJustification.removedPrefix: Events 1375–1385 were removed because they contain the question transition, denial of obsession, and setup about choosing a familiar difficult example, not the evidence itself.
boundaryJustification.removedSuffix: Event 1475 was removed because it is only a transition about remaining speaking time after the evolution conclusion is complete at event 1474.

repairs.longerCompleteArgumentRationale: The span exceeds 2200 characters because separated components are indispensable: events 1386–1392 supply the proposed multiple pathways for gaining eyes; events 1417–1429 supply the cave salamander's eye-shaped vestiges and loss; events 1441–1449 explain the infection-related disadvantage; and events 1456–1474 explain non-intentional selection through survival and breeding. Removing either endpoint would drop a named reason or the completed mechanism, while the intervening events connect these components as one continuous gain-and-loss adaptation argument.

limitations: Only the assigned evidence-04 source excerpt was read; no full-debate read was performed.
